stem: How does Prometheus normally collect metrics from targets?

options.text: It pulls them over HTTP on a schedule
options.note: Right. Collection happens through a pull model over HTTP.

options.text: Targets push metrics to the Prometheus server
options.note: Pushing is only supported through an intermediary, the Pushgateway, and only for limited cases.

options.text: It reads targets' log files
options.note: Prometheus is a metrics system. It doesn't read logs.

options.text: Through a message queue such as Kafka
options.note: There's no message queue in the standard collection path.

explanation: Prometheus features include time series collection via a pull model over HTTP, with pushing supported via an intermediary gateway.

sources.title: FAQ › Why do you pull rather than push?

stem: Which are advantages of pulling that the Prometheus FAQ lists? Select all that apply.

options.text: You can start extra monitoring instances as needed, for example on a laptop
options.note: Right. Targets don't need to know who's scraping them.

options.text: You can more easily and reliably tell when a target is down
options.note: Right. A failed scrape is a clear signal.

options.text: You can manually inspect a target's health in a web browser
options.note: Right. Just open its metrics endpoint.

options.text: Pull guarantees 100% accurate data for billing
options.note: The docs say Prometheus isn't suited to 100% accuracy needs such as billing.

explanation: The FAQ lists three advantages: extra monitoring instances are easy to start, target-down detection is easier and more reliable, and targets can be inspected manually with a browser.
hint: One option makes a claim the docs explicitly reject elsewhere.

sources.title: FAQ › Why do you pull rather than push?

stem: How strongly does the Prometheus FAQ rate pull over push?

options.text: Slightly better. It shouldn't be a major point when choosing a monitoring system
options.note: Right. The FAQ is deliberately modest about it.

options.text: Push is fundamentally broken and should never be used
options.note: The FAQ doesn't say that. It offers the Pushgateway for cases where you must push.

options.text: Pull is the single most important feature of Prometheus
options.note: The FAQ says the opposite: it shouldn't be a major consideration.

options.text: They are exactly equivalent in every way
options.note: The FAQ does think pull is slightly better, for the reasons it lists.

explanation: The FAQ says that overall pulling is slightly better than pushing, but it should not be considered a major point when choosing a monitoring system.

sources.title: FAQ › Why do you pull rather than push?

stem: A target's scrape fails. What value does Prometheus record for up{job="api", instance="10.0.0.5:8080"}?

options.note: Right. up is 1 when the instance is reachable and healthy, 0 when the scrape failed.
1 means the scrape succeeded.

options.text: No sample is recorded at all
options.note: Prometheus records up on every scrape attempt, which is what makes it useful for spotting failures.

options.text: NaN
options.note: up is explicitly 1 or 0.

explanation: For each instance scrape, Prometheus stores `up` as 1 if the instance is healthy (reachable) or 0 if the scrape failed.

sources.title: Jobs and instances › Automatically generated labels and time series

stem: According to the docs, what is usually the only valid use case for the Pushgateway?

options.text: Capturing the outcome of a service-level batch job
options.note: Right. A job not tied to a specific machine or instance, such as a cleanup job for a whole service.

options.text: Collecting metrics from all long-running web services
options.note: Long-running services should be scraped. The docs warn against using the Pushgateway for general collection.

options.text: Getting metrics through a firewall from many hosts
options.note: For firewalls the docs suggest running Prometheus inside the network, or PushProx.

options.text: Batch jobs that run on, and relate to, one particular machine
options.note: Machine-related batch jobs should use the Node Exporter textfile collector instead.

explanation: The docs say the only valid use case for the Pushgateway is usually capturing the outcome of a service-level batch job, one not semantically related to a specific machine or instance.
hint: Which kind of batch job isn't tied to any one machine?

sources.title: When to use the Pushgateway › Should I be using the Pushgateway?

stem: Which are pitfalls of using the Pushgateway for general metrics collection? Select all that apply.

options.text: It can become a single point of failure and a bottleneck
options.note: Right. Many instances funnel through one gateway.

options.text: You lose automatic health monitoring via the up metric
options.note: Right. Prometheus scrapes the gateway, not your instances.

options.text: Pushed series stay forever unless deleted through its API
options.note: Right. The gateway's lifecycle is separate from the processes that push to it.

options.text: It can't accept metrics in the Prometheus text format
options.note: It does accept the text format. Even shell scripts can push with it.

explanation: The docs list three pitfalls: a single point of failure and bottleneck, loss of the `up` metric, and series that are never forgotten unless manually deleted.
hint: Three of these come straight from the 'Should I be using the Pushgateway?' section.

sources.title: When to use the Pushgateway › Should I be using the Pushgateway?

stem: A batch job instance pushed metrics to the Pushgateway, then was removed from service. What happens to its metrics?

options.text: They stay in the Pushgateway and keep being exposed until someone deletes them
options.note: Right. The Pushgateway never forgets pushed series on its own.

options.text: They disappear automatically after the next scrape
options.note: That's how pull-based targets behave. The Pushgateway keeps series indefinitely.

options.text: They expire after the default 5-minute timeout
options.note: There's no such timeout. Series stay until manually deleted.

options.text: Prometheus marks them with up=0
options.note: There's no up for pushed jobs. That's one of the pitfalls.

explanation: The Pushgateway never forgets series pushed to it and exposes them to Prometheus forever unless they're manually deleted via its API.
hint: Compare this with what happens when a scraped target disappears.

sources.title: When to use the Pushgateway › Should I be using the Pushgateway?

stem: Your targets sit behind a NAT, and Prometheus can't reach them to scrape. What do the docs recommend first?

options.text: Run the Prometheus server on the same network, behind the barrier
options.note: Right. The docs generally recommend running Prometheus on the same network as the monitored instances.

options.text: Have every target push to a central Pushgateway
options.note: That brings back all the Pushgateway pitfalls. It isn't the recommended fix.

options.text: Increase the scrape timeout
options.note: A longer timeout doesn't help if the network path doesn't exist.

options.text: Switch to reading logs instead
options.note: That changes the signal entirely rather than solving the network problem.

explanation: If a firewall or NAT prevents pulling, move the Prometheus server behind the network barrier as well. Otherwise consider PushProx, which lets Prometheus traverse a firewall or NAT.
hint: Bring the scraper closer to the targets.

sources.title: When to use the Pushgateway › Alternative strategies

stem: A nightly cron job on each host applies security updates. How should you expose its results?

options.text: Write them for the Node Exporter textfile collector on that host
options.note: Right. Machine-related batch jobs should use the textfile collector.

options.text: Push them to a shared Pushgateway with an instance label
options.note: Machine-tied results in the Pushgateway hit the 'never forgets' problem when hosts are renamed or removed.

options.text: Add a recording rule
options.note: Recording rules compute from existing data. They don't expose new data from a cron job.

options.text: Send them to Alertmanager
options.note: Alertmanager handles alerts, not metrics.

explanation: For batch jobs related to a machine, such as security update cron jobs, expose the results using the Node Exporter's textfile collector instead of the Pushgateway.
hint: The job belongs to one machine, and something already runs on that machine to expose its metrics.

sources.title: When to use the Pushgateway › Alternative strategies

stem: Why do short-lived batch jobs often need the Pushgateway rather than being scraped?

options.text: They may finish and exit before Prometheus would ever scrape them
options.note: Right. You can't scrape a process that's no longer running.

options.text: Batch jobs can't use client libraries
options.note: They can. The issue is lifetime, not libraries.

options.text: Prometheus refuses to scrape batch jobs
options.note: There's no such restriction. Long-running batch jobs can be scraped too.

options.text: Batch job metrics are always gauges
options.note: Type isn't the reason. The short lifetime is.

explanation: Batch jobs don't run continuously, which makes scraping them difficult. The Pushgateway lets them push metrics that Prometheus can scrape after they've terminated.
